observations: 38 API operations identified across 2 protocols: REST (staging-api.teeinblue.com, 24 operations) and GraphQL (staging-graphql.teeinblue.com/v1/graphql, 14 operations).

No plain REST list endpoint (GET /api/campaigns or GET /api/platform-products) was found anywhere in the 18 captures -- FEAT-03 list/browse is served entirely via GraphQL (APIOP-032, APIOP-034), confirmed by full request/response inspection, not inferred from naming.

by-product-base flow's core 'add product to campaign' mutation is GraphQL insert_campaign_products (APIOP-027); the REST POST /api/staff-activity-logs/campaign-product observed alongside it is only an activity-log side effect, not the data write itself.

by-product-base uses a printarea-scoped artwork assignment (POST /api/campaign-artworks/batch-apply-to-printareas, APIOP-008) while by-shopify uses a flat artwork assignment with no printarea concept (POST /api/platform-artworks, APIOP-016) -- matches the print-area vs. no-print-area UI difference already noted by portal-explorer.

by-shopify's 'No mockup' validation is resolved by a dedicated POST /api/platform-products/{id}/platform-mockups (APIOP-022) call with no equivalent in by-product-base (which derives its mockup readiness from the product-base print-area mockups generated via APIOP-006/007).

Publish mechanics differ at the request-shape level, not just UI: by-product-base's publish (APIOP-010) requires a body {instance_id} (one store per call, matching the per-row Launch button in the Multi-store launch dialog); by-shopify's publish (APIOP-023) takes no body at all (store is fixed at creation time).
assumptions: Where a GraphQL query's `where` filter (e.g. campaign_id, status) is embedded directly in the query text rather than passed as a variable, this is treated as an implementation/codegen detail, not confirmed server-side behavior.

security_surfaces.surface: Cross-store / org-level visibility in Multi-store launch (GraphQL instances / instances_aggregate)
security_surfaces.note: Owner-level GraphQL query for the launch dialog returns ALL stores in the Organization (linh-explorer AND linh-explorer-2), including a store explicitly outside this run's allowed account scope. The actual mutating publish call (POST /api/campaigns/{id}/publish) was correctly restricted by the human operator to only the allowed store, but the READ surface itself exposes org-wide store list+domain+sync-status to any owner session. Worth a dedicated tenant-isolation/permission test on this GraphQL query and on POST publish body validation (does the API itself reject an instance_id outside the caller's allowed scope, or does it rely entirely on UI restraint?) -- NOT tested this run.
